html:
The kingdom of Syphax was the realm of the Masaesyli, a Berber people of western Numidia, in what is now western and central Algeria. Its capital was Siga, near the coast. It is shown here in 200 BCE.

Syphax was its king during the Second Punic War, and both Carthage and Rome courted him. He sided with Rome at first, then switched to Carthage and married Sophonisba, daughter of a Carthaginian general. His rival was Masinissa, prince of the eastern Numidians, the kingdom of Gala.

When Scipio Africanus invaded Africa, Roman troops and Masinissa beat Syphax in 203 BCE and took him prisoner. He died in captivity in Italy. Masinissa took his lands and united all of Numidia.
